key_insight: The paper splits the kinetic solution into a local-equilibrium “wave” and a non-equilibrium “particle,” creating a continuous bridge from full kinetic transport to Navier-Stokes hydrodynamics that adapts cell-by-cell.
engineering_relevance: This framework can accelerate multiscale flow solvers by using macroscopic updates where the flow is near equilibrium and kinetic updates only where non-equilibrium transport is important.
method: Define a wave from the equilibrium integral over a local kinetic horizon and a particle as its exact complement.
Derive coupled evolution equations whose moments recover extended Navier-Stokes-type systems and remain equivalent to the original kinetic equation.
Use a steady-state coupled wave-particle iteration: alternate a macroscopic solve for conservative variables with a kinetic solve for the particle.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports hypersonic cylinder and 3D X38 vehicle simulations, showing flow-adaptive decomposition and strong iteration acceleration.
watch_item: Performance and robustness depend on choosing an appropriate horizon-to-relaxation ratio, and the particle update may still be costly in strongly non-equilibrium regions.
paper_title: A wave-particle decomposition framework for multiscale kinetic transport: continuous-spectrum equations and coupled wave-particle iteration
